angle: An octopus has nine brains and can taste with its arms
title: This Animal Has 9 Brains (and Tastes With Its Arms)
description: Octopuses have a central brain plus a mini-brain in every arm.

scenes.narration: This animal has nine brains, and it tastes with its arms.
Meet the octopus. Two thirds of its neurons are not in its head at all.

visual.label: of neurons live in the arms

scenes.narration: Each arm has its own cluster of nerves that can make decisions without asking the central brain.

scenes.narration: Their suckers are packed with chemical receptors, so touching a rock is also tasting it.
Brain versus arms: the central brain sets the goal, the arms work out the details.
Scientists have watched them open jars, escape tanks and even recognise human faces.
Picture the nervous system as a machine: one hub, eight independent processors.
Their family tree split from ours more than five hundred million years ago.
As one researcher put it, an octopus is the closest we'll get to meeting an alien. Nine brains, and it tastes with its arms. Follow for more like this.
